title: Qadrant · Your tasks, sorted on your phone
description: An agenda built on the Eisenhower matrix. Type or say a task and Qadrant places it in Do, Schedule, Delegate or Eliminate. Runs on your device.
heroTitle: Say what you have to do. Qadrant decides where it goes.
heroLead: Type or dictate a task in plain words. Qadrant reads the date, works out whether it is urgent and whether it matters to your goals, and places it in Do, Schedule, Delegate or Eliminate.
heroFine: Free. No account. Your tasks stay on your phone.
mockTask: Send the quarterly report by tomorrow
step1Title: Write it as you would say it
step1Text: “Call the dentist on Monday”, “Ask Laura to book the room”. No forms, no fields to fill in. You can also dictate it.
step2Text: It shows why: the date it found, the goal it relates to and how sure it is. When it is unsure, it asks you a single yes or no question.
step3Text: Change the quadrant with one tap. Every correction is kept, so the next proposals fit you better.
matrixLead: The Eisenhower matrix splits work by two questions: is it urgent, and is it important? Qadrant answers them for you and keeps the answer up to date as dates get closer.
qDoText: What cannot wait and matters. It goes first, before its deadline.
qScheduleText: What moves you forward. Give it time before it becomes urgent; when its date comes close, it moves to Do by itself.
qDelegateText: What someone else can do. Qadrant remembers who has it and when to follow up.
qEliminateText: What you can let go. After two weeks untouched, Qadrant suggests archiving it.
privateLead: Qadrant is local-first. There is no Qadrant account and no Qadrant server holding your tasks.
f1Text: Everything is stored in your browser on your device. No analytics, no tracking, no third-party calls.
f2Title: The assistant runs on your phone
f2Text: A small multilingual model downloads once, over wifi if you like, and sorts your tasks without sending them anywhere.
f3Text: Before the model is downloaded, or if your phone cannot run it, Qadrant sorts with rules and you choose by hand.
f4Text: Install it as an app and it opens with no connection, on the train or on a plane.
f5Text: It understands tasks in both languages, dates included: “next Friday” or “el viernes que viene”.
f6Text: Export all your tasks to a file whenever you want, and import them on another device.
installLead: Qadrant is a web app you add to your home screen. No app store, no updates to approve.
iosText: Open Qadrant in Safari, tap Share and then “Add to Home Screen”. Installing it also stops iOS from clearing your tasks after days without a visit.
androidText: Open Qadrant in Chrome and tap “Install app” in the menu, or accept the install banner when it appears.
desktopText: In Chrome or Edge, use the install icon in the address bar. It also works as a normal tab in any modern browser.
syncTitle: Same tasks on every device, on your own server
syncLead: If you want sync and reminders, run the open-source Qadrant server on your own machine. You keep the data; Qadrant never sees it.
closingTitle: Clear your head in ten seconds
closingLead: Write the first thing on your mind and see where it lands.
